messages:
julia: quick heads-up — after yesterday's shard rebalance I noticed a steady decline in prefix-cache hit rate on the canary cluster (node-pool B).

mike: is this live traffic or the replay harness you ran?

julia: replay with production traces (90p seq len). baseline before rebalance: ~85% hit. after rebalance: ~67%. timeline matches the rollout window.

srinivas: hmm, that sounds like cohort mapping changed and prefixes got split across more shards. can you paste the small diff you applied to the slot allocator?

julia: sure — short snippet from the change:

```diff
-   slot_count = compute_slots(old_layout)
+   slot_count = compute_slots(new_layout, include_replicas=True)
```

julia: not huge but might change hot-key placement.

ana: curious whether the KV occupancy skew metric moved too. can you run a quick occupancy histogram and a prefix-length CDF? if skew increased then more misses are expected.

mike: also check the eviction tail — if we pushed more keys into fewer slots that could cause earlier TTL-driven evictions for those slots.

julia: running quick probe now — will post numbers in ~10m. can someone spin the replay at 1x and 5x so we can compare throughput sensitivity? i don't want to mask misses with batching.

ci-bot: load-test/bench-replay started by julia at 1928888930 — replay-id: r-2026-04-kv-decay-01

srinivas: i'll take the profiling slice for node-pool B — sampling CPU and cache-ops counters. should have a flame + kv-op histogram in ~15m.

lauren: FYI i queued a small canary rollback PR in case we need to revert the allocator tweak quickly: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/4523 — tagging @mike @srinivas

mike: thanks. after we have occupancy + profiling let's decide: (A) live rollback, (B) tune allocator to preserve previous hot-key groupings, or (C) add a transient pre-warm step during rebalance to avoid cold misses.

julia: occupancy histogram attached (summary): slot skew Gini went from 0.12 -> 0.31, hot 5% slots now contain ~42% of keys. prefix length CDF shows a small shift toward longer prefixes (more unique prefixes post-reshard).

ana: that Gini is significant. i vote pre-warm approach (C) — it's lower risk than rollback and avoids oscillation on retries.

srinivas: pre-warm implementation idea: after slot remap, schedule a background replay of top-N prefixes per slot with low-priority batching and KV prefetching. can reuse the existing warmup worker with throttling.

mike: good plan. julia — can you open a tiny work item with steps + perf acceptance criteria (target: restore hit rate to >=82% within 10m of completion) and assign to srinivas? add CI replay id and a link to rollback PR.

julia: done — https://tickets.internal/redwood/INF-1289 (assigned srinivas). added bench replay r-2026-04-kv-decay-01 and rollback PR link. acceptance: 82%+ hit at 90p seq len within 10m of warmup end, no >3% latency tail increase.

srinivas: ack. i'll prototype pre-warm patch, run a controlled replay, and post results. ping me if you see any error logs from warmup workers.

lauren: i'll hold the rollback until we see profiling. if we need to revert, i'll merge the PR and schedule a safe window.

mike: thanks all. follow-ups: julia post raw replay artifacts, srinivas post flame + kv-op histogram, lauren hold rollback. we'll regroup in this thread in ~30m.

julia: artifact links: s3://bench-archive/r-2026-04-kv-decay-01/{replay.log,occupancy.json}. i'm also uploading the raw trace slice.

srinivas: initial profiling output: increased cache-lookup latency on affected nodes, and a 2.3x increase in miss-path CPU. starting pre-warm run now (id: warm-01).

ci-bot: warmup/job warm-01 started at 1928889360

julia: pre-warm results: hit rate after warm-01: 83.1% (90p seq len). latency tail stable. warm-01 consumed ~2% extra tokens during warmup window.

ana: awesome — looks like pre-warm is effective. can we make it opt-in during rebalances until we bake more confidence?

srinivas: i'll open a follow-up PR with flags and safe defaults. also adding a metric to track warmup effectiveness per rebalance.

mike: perfect. closing the loop: no rollback, proceed with opt-in pre-warm, monitor for 24h. thanks team :thumbsup:
